name: Profhilo Body

lead: Profhilo Body is an IBSA injectable hyaluronic acid product used by clinicians to treat skin laxity and roughness on areas like the upper arms and hands.
A 12-month single-arm study and a completed hands trial exist, but no controlled comparisons were found.

paras: It uses hybrid complexes of high- and low-molecular-weight hyaluronic acid injected into the skin, intended to improve skin quality rather than add bulk.
A post-marketing review has assessed adverse event reports for the product family. Injection procedures carry general risks such as bruising and swelling, and it is given by trained clinicians.

lead: Profhilo Body is an injectable hybrid hyaluronic acid (HA) product from IBSA Farmaceutici, marketed as a medical device for improving skin laxity and roughness on the body, such as the upper inner arms and the backs of the hands. It uses the NAHYCO hybrid technology, which forms cooperative complexes from high- and low-molecular-weight HA.[1]

Published evidence includes a 12-month single-arm study of women with upper-arm skin laxity, a registered trial on the backs of the hands, and a post-marketing safety review of hybrid cooperative complex HA products used on the face and body.[1][2][3] These are small and mostly uncontrolled.
infobox: Body skin laxity, e.g. upper inner arms, hands

paras: Profhilo Body is the body-oriented formulation in the Profhilo range. It is described in the literature as a "skin booster" intended to improve skin quality rather than to add volume.[1][2]

A single-centre, single-arm study over 12 months treated women aged 37 to 65 with at least initial signs of laxity and roughness of the upper arms. The schedule was two injection sessions one month apart followed by five sessions two months apart, with follow-up evaluation. The authors reported on long-term safety and efficacy.[2]

A registered trial, NCT05590364, assessed an intradermal injectable treatment for skin roughness and laxity on the backs of the hands in 51 participants and is listed as completed.[3] Results were not available in the sources reviewed.
No randomised controlled trials of Profhilo Body versus a control were identified in the sources reviewed.

A 2025 review analysed post-marketing adverse events for hybrid cooperative complex HA injected into the face (reporting from 2018 to 2023) and the body, to update its safety profile after nearly ten years of use.[1] The review is based on spontaneous reports rather than controlled comparison.
